channel.title: nanoMMO | Building nanoMMO: The Engineering Series
channel.description: An MMO built from scratch, with the focus on the engineering around the game.

item.title: Episode 42: MMORPG loot tables and drops on a C++ server
item.description: Monsters drop loot from tables in the content, each item with its chance, into the killer's bag, the chat says what dropped, and the bots drink and dress.

item.title: Episode 41: Drag and drop MMORPG inventory with Dear ImGui
item.description: The server sends each player their bag and takes what they do with it, and the client draws it, with icons, tooltips, drag and drop, and the slots that are worn.

item.title: Episode 40: Saving MMO inventories with Redis and MySQL
item.description: Each player carries a bag and fights with what they wear, drinks potions with a cooldown, and has their bag saved, through Redis to MySQL, when it changes.

item.title: Episode 39: A data-driven item system for an MMO game server
item.description: Items made of parts instead of types, with stacks, equipment slots, stats, potions and rolls, and a bag to carry them in, which a property test plays with twenty thousand times.

item.title: Episode 38: Instanced dungeons for an MMORPG game server
item.description: The Crypt, a dungeon that gives each player who goes in a copy of it of their own, with copies that go once they're empty, and players saved outside it.

item.title: Episode 37: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner: deploy on push
item.description: A GitHub Actions runner on our server, in Docker, deploys each push to main once CI passes, with the worlds handing their players over, and refuses any other job.

item.title: Episode 36: Zero downtime deploys for an MMORPG game server
item.description: A world that hands its players over to its next instance before it stops, through Consul, with a token for each move, so a deploy no longer throws anyone out.

item.title: Episode 35: Game server logs with Grafana Loki and Alloy
item.description: The servers' logs in Loki, collected by Alloy from Docker, labelled by service and stream, on the dashboard next to the metrics, and an alert from the logs.

item.title: Episode 34: MMORPG skill trainer NPC with MySQL and Redis
item.description: A trainer that teaches the skills, from their levels on, checked on the server, asked for in a window of its own, and saved through Redis to a table in MySQL.

item.title: Episode 33: Bloom and cel shading in C++ with raylib
item.description: Bloom from raylib's post-processing example, done the way games do it, with a frame of floats and lava that gives off light, then cel shading from raylib's example, FXAA, and settings for them.

item.title: Episode 32: Game music in C++ with raylib audio
item.description: Music in the world with raylib's audio, streamed and refilled each frame, faded in and out by a jukebox, with volume sliders in decibels and settings that the client keeps.

item.title: Episode 31: MMORPG skills, cooldowns and a hotbar in C++
item.description: Four skills as content, used on the server with a level and a cooldown each, a hotbar on the number keys, animations from Mixamo, and a camera that tilts.

item.title: Episode 30: Prometheus Alertmanager: alert rules and email
item.description: Prometheus alerts when a world falls behind or goes down, Alertmanager emails each alert to a mail server in Docker, and promtool tests the rules.

item.title: Episode 29: Integration testing a C++ game server
item.description: A test starts the world server on port zero and plays it over TLS, UBSan catches the test's own bug, and the coverage report sees the game loop run.

item.title: Episode 28: C++ sanitizers, fuzzing and coverage in Docker
item.description: Sanitizers under the bots, fuzzing, clang-tidy and a coverage report find what the tests don't, and we fix it.

item.title: Episode 27: Data-driven MMO content in C++ with protobuf
item.description: Monsters and NPCs join the items as data both sides read, go out by kind, and a content hash keeps clients and worlds in step.

item.title: Episode 26: MMO items in C++ with protobuf text format
item.description: Our sword moves out of code into one items file, in protobuf's text format, which both the server and the client read, each taking the part it needs.

item.title: Episode 25: An LLM-powered NPC in a C++ MMO server
item.description: A storyteller NPC writes players a story from a few words, with a small language model served next to the game, asked from threads off the tick.

item.title: Episode 24: MMO NPCs in C++: data-driven, low bandwidth
item.description: Our first NPCs, as tables of kinds and spawns, sent once a second and drawn as coloured balls until they have models.

item.title: Episode 23: MMO chat in C++: TCP, ImGui and rate limits
item.description: Players talk to everyone in their world, over TCP, with each line cleaned on the server and a token bucket against floods.

item.title: Episode 22: MMO zones and portals in C++ with raylib
item.description: Each world gets a second land, the Ashlands, with a gate from the Meadows, and each land a look of its own, as data.

item.title: Episode 21: Consul service discovery for a C++ game server
item.description: Each game server is a world that registers with Consul, the client lists the worlds through the login server, and each world keeps its own players.

item.title: Episode 20: MMO interest management: send each player less
item.description: Each player gets the players near them, in cells of the island, and names and levels once a second, measured change by change, on my machine and on the VPS.

item.title: Episode 19: Deploy a C++ game server to a VPS with Docker
item.description: Our game goes onto a VPS, deployed over SSH with Docker Compose, with the database kept private and certificates for the server's address.

item.title: Episode 18: MySQL schema migrations with Flyway in Docker
item.description: Flyway keeps our MySQL tables in versions, so a change to them keeps the players' accounts, starting with saving their health.

item.title: Episode 17: Game character screen in C++ with raylib, ImGui
item.description: A character screen with our player's details next to an idle 3D preview, which a camera of its own draws into a render texture for Dear ImGui to show.

item.title: Episode 16: Trees and frustum culling in C++ with raylib
item.description: Trees grow on the island where the seed says, the server makes their trunks solid, and chunks with culling make the client a lot faster.

item.title: Episode 15: Procedural terrain in C++ with noise and raylib
item.description: Our board of tiles becomes an island 512 metres across, from noise and a seed that the server and the client share, with a camera that follows you.

item.title: Episode 14: TLS for a C++ game server with OpenSSL and Asio
item.description: Our client sends the password, and gets its token back, as plain bytes, so we put TLS 1.3 on all our TCP connections, with OpenSSL, Asio and a certificate authority of our own.

item.title: Episode 13: Redis cache in C++: write-behind to MySQL
item.description: Saving each change to MySQL slows our server down with a few dozen players, so we put Redis in between, with a pipeline, an append-only file and a saver that writes to MySQL in batches.

item.title: Episode 12: Laravel game website in Docker: login, rankings
item.description: A Laravel website next to the game, in Docker, with rankings, and accounts that log into the game, on the game's own MySQL tables, with no CSS of our own.

item.title: Episode 11: C++ MMO combat: swords, hits and respawns
item.description: A public-domain sword in each hand, swings the server decides, and monsters that fight back, with a death animation for both.

item.title: Episode 10: C++ MMO monsters: AI, health and levels
item.description: A public-domain skeleton, monsters with an AI on the server, and health, levels and experience for everyone.

item.title: Episode 9: TCP vs UDP for a game server, under packet loss
item.description: We make the network drop packets, measure how old the world on a player's screen gets over TCP and then over UDP, and let the numbers decide.

item.title: Episode 8: Profiling a C++ game server with perf and Tracy
item.description: We step the bots up until the server falls behind, find out where its time goes with perf, flame graphs and Tracy, fix the broadcast, and measure it again.

item.title: Episode 7: raylib 3D animation in C++: Mixamo and glTF
item.description: Mixamo characters converted to glTF, merged into files raylib can load, synced through the server and skinned on the GPU.

item.title: Episode 6: C++ login server with Redis tokens
item.description: A login server checks passwords away from the game server's tick, and hands each login over through Redis as a one-time token.

item.title: Episode 5: C++ game accounts with MySQL and Argon2id
item.description: Players get accounts, kept in MySQL through its C API, with their passwords hashed with Argon2id.

item.title: Episode 4: Prometheus and Grafana for a C++ game server
item.description: Our server reports metrics, Prometheus collects them, Grafana draws them, Docker Compose starts it all, and three hundred bots give it something to show.

item.title: Episode 3: C++ multiplayer with protobuf and Asio
item.description: A C++ server keeps several clients in sync, over TCP, with a protobuf contract between them.

item.title: Episode 2: C++ game client with raylib, ImGui and shaders
item.description: The client's first window, drawn with raylib, with Dear ImGui on top, tests that run in Docker without a screen or a GPU, and a cube that the keyboard moves.

item.title: Episode 1: How to build an MMORPG from scratch in C++
item.description: Where the series is going, and a C++ project that is built, tested and documented on each push.
